question: Can supported Dolt 2.3.2 privilege or connection configuration prevent the normal application identity from changing session or global dolt_force_transaction_commit while preserving required TaskStore writes?

environment.operating_system: Linux 6.12.107+deb13-amd64 #1 SMP PREEMPT_DYNAMIC Debian 6.12.107-1 (2026-08-29) x86_64 GNU/Linux
environment.topology: one disposable loopback SQL server; system_variables and per-user user_session_vars initialize dolt_force_transaction_commit to 0; one owner and one table-scoped application identity

supported_controls.read_only_rejected_as_boundary: The public behavior.read_only control disables database modification, including required TaskStore INSERT and UPDATE operations.

grants: GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE ON `force_boundary_c29a0732c2a27c60`.`aggregates` TO `app_c29a0732c2a27c60`@`%`

decision.residual: The trusted engine identity can override both configured safe values; deliberate compromise of that identity is outside the database boundary.
decision.required_adapter_control: Set and verify session and global dolt_force_transaction_commit=0 before writes and fail closed on any error or drift.
